facts: LABOUR DEPARTMENT OF GHANA FACT SHEET (general guidance; Labour Act 2003, Act 651 is authoritative).
Parent ministry: Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment. Toll-free 0800 600 300 / 0800 600 400. Website melr.gov.gh.
Chief Labour Officer: Braimah Ibrahim Dawuda.

Offices: Mon-Fri 8:00-17:00. Public Employment Centres (PECs) in all 16 regions (e.g. Odomase, Bono Region; Goaso, Ahafo Region). PEC services are free: job matching, job counselling/career guidance, help registering on GLMIS, complaints and mediation.

GLMIS (Ghana Labour Market Information System), https://www.glmis.gov.gh: free government jobs portal. Job seekers create a profile, upload CV, apply for vacancies. Employers post vacancies and search candidates free. Publishes labour market information. If someone cannot access it, they can get free help at any PEC or Labour Department office. Always recommend GLMIS for job, vacancy, CV or unemployment questions.
Minimum wage: National Daily Minimum Wage {{minWageYear}} is GH¢{{minWage}}/day, effective {{minWageEffective}} ({{prevMinWageYear}}: GH¢{{prevMinWage}}). Set by the National Tripartite Committee.
Annual leave: at least 15 working days with full pay after 12 months continuous service (s.20 Act 651).
Hours: normal maximum 8 hours/day, 40 hours/week. Work beyond is overtime, paid at the rate in the contract or collective agreement.

Maternity: at least 12 weeks leave on full pay, plus 2 extra weeks for abnormal delivery or multiple births. Nursing mothers may take nursing breaks during working hours. Dismissal for pregnancy is unfair.
Written terms: for work of 6 months or more, employer gives written statement of main terms within 2 months.
Termination notice (or pay in lieu): contract 3 years or more: 1 month; under 3 years: 2 weeks; week-to-week: 7 days.
Unfair termination: e.g. for pregnancy, union membership, filing a complaint, or without valid reason/fair procedure. Report to the nearest Labour Department office for free mediation; act promptly.
Complaints process: 1) raise with employer, in writing; 2) nearest Labour Department office or PEC for advice and free mediation; 3) if no agreement, the Labour Officer advises on further options.

Child labour (Children's Act 1998, Act 560): minimum employment age 15; light work from 13; hazardous work (mining, galamsey, fishing at sea, heavy loads, chemicals) 18; no night work for children 8pm-6am. Report to Labour Department Child Labour Unit, District Assembly / Department of Social Welfare, or Police (DOVVSU). Ghana Accelerated Action Plan Against Child Labour 2023-2027.

Workmen's compensation (Workmen's Compensation Law 1987, PNDCL 187): employer reports work accident to Labour Department; worker gets medical assessment; Department assesses claim; employer or its insurer pays.

Occupational safety: employer must provide safe workplace, training and PPE at no cost; workers can report unsafe conditions. Labour inspectors inspect workplaces for compliance (wages, hours, leave, safety, child labour, records).

Private employment agency licensing: register company with Registrar-General; apply to the Minister through the Labour Department; inspection of premises and staff; licence issued; quarterly returns within 14 days after each quarter. Operating unlicensed is illegal.

Recruitment scams / jobs abroad: only use licensed agencies; never pay for 'visa lottery' or guaranteed jobs; get a written contract before travel; do not surrender passport to unverified agents; verify agencies with the Labour Department.
Trade unions: workers may form or join a union; punishing union membership is unfair.
New Labour Bill: in progress, NOT yet law; would cover gig/platform and remote work. Act 651 still applies.
Contacts: info@labourdepartment.gov.gh. Website labourdepartment.gov.gh. Blog at /blog.
Site pages: /blog, /glmis, /services, /services#complaints, /services#agencies, /services#compensation, /workers-rights, /employers, /child-labour, /faq, /contact, /about.

questions: what is the ghana labour market information system
intents.answer:
**GLMIS** (Ghana Labour Market Information System) is the government's free online jobs platform. It connects job seekers with employers across Ghana and publishes labour market information.

-   Job seekers create a profile, upload a CV and apply for vacancies
-   Employers post vacancies and search for candidates
-   Anyone can view labour market data and trends

questions: how do i get a job
how to register as a job seeker
intents.answer:
The fastest way is to **register on GLMIS**, Ghana's free government jobs portal:

-   Open the [GLMIS sign-up page](https://www.glmis.gov.gh/Identity/Account/Register) and create a job seeker account
-   Complete your profile, skills and upload your CV
-   Search and apply for vacancies, and let employers find you

You can also visit a **Public Employment Centre** in your region for free job matching and counselling.

questions: how do i post a vacancy
intents.answer:
Employers can recruit for free on **GLMIS**:

-   Create an employer account on the [GLMIS company sign-up page](https://www.glmis.gov.gh/Identity/Account/RegisterCompany)
-   Post your vacancy with the job description and requirements
-   Search job seeker profiles and shortlist candidates

The Public Employment Centre in your region can also help match you with suitable candidates.

questions: do i pay to register on glmis
is there a fee for glmis
intents.answer:
Yes. **GLMIS is free** for both job seekers and employers. Services at the Public Employment Centres are also free.

Never pay anyone who asks for money to register you or "guarantee" a job.

questions: i do not have internet to register
intents.answer:
If you have trouble with GLMIS:

-   Use the password reset option on the GLMIS login page
-   Try another browser or device, or a different network
-   Visit your nearest **Public Employment Centre** or Labour Department office. Staff can help you register and update your profile for free

questions: where can i find labour market data
intents.answer:
Labour market information (vacancy trends, in-demand skills and related data) is published on **GLMIS**. It is useful for job seekers choosing a career, employers planning hiring and researchers.

For official national employment statistics you can also check the Ghana Statistical Service.

questions: how do i write a cv
how to prepare for an interview
intents.answer:
Tips for a strong application:

-   Keep your CV to 1 or 2 pages: contact details, skills, experience, education
-   Tailor it to each vacancy and use clear job titles
-   Upload it to your **GLMIS** profile so employers can find you

For free one-on-one career guidance, visit a **Public Employment Centre**.

questions: what is a public employment centre
is there a labour office in my region
intents.answer:
**Public Employment Centres (PECs)** are Labour Department offices in all 16 regions, for example at Odomase (Bono Region) and Goaso (Ahafo Region). Their services are **free**:

-   Job matching and placement
-   Job counselling and career guidance
-   Help registering on GLMIS
-   Labour complaints and mediation

questions: i do not know what job to do
intents.answer:
Yes. Our Public Employment Centres offer **free job counselling**: help choosing a career, matching your skills to available work and preparing for interviews.

Register on GLMIS too, so you see current vacancies.

questions: how much is minimum wage now
what is the minimum wage in 2026
intents.answer:
The **National Daily Minimum Wage for {{minWageYear}} is GH¢{{minWage}}** per day, effective **{{minWageEffective}}**. In {{prevMinWageYear}} it was GH¢{{prevMinWage}}.

It is set by the National Tripartite Committee (government, employers and organised labour). No employer may pay a worker below it.

questions: my employer has not paid my salary
my boss is not paying me
they owe me money for work
pay day passed and no salary
intents.answer:
Your employer must pay your wages in full and on time, as agreed in your contract. If wages are unpaid or wrongly deducted:

-   Raise it with your employer in writing first and keep copies
-   If it is not resolved, report to the nearest **Labour Department office** for mediation
-   The Labour Officer will invite your employer and help you both reach a settlement

questions: how many leave days do i get
am i entitled to annual leave
intents.answer:
Under section 20 of the Labour Act (Act 651), a worker is entitled to **at least 15 working days of paid annual leave** after **12 months of continuous service**.

Your contract or collective agreement may give more. Leave cannot be given up for money, except where the law or agreement allows.

questions: how many hours should i work
my boss makes me work 12 hours
intents.answer:
The normal maximum is **8 hours a day** and **40 hours a week**. Work beyond these hours is **overtime** and must be paid at the agreed overtime rate.

If you are regularly made to work longer without overtime pay, report it to the Labour Department.

questions: do i get paid for overtime
can my employer force me to work overtime
intents.answer:
Work beyond 8 hours a day or 40 hours a week is **overtime**. It should be paid at the rate set in your contract or collective agreement.

If overtime is not being paid, keep a record of your hours and report to the nearest Labour Department office.

questions: am i paid during maternity leave
intents.answer:
A woman worker is entitled to **at least 12 weeks of maternity leave on full pay**, plus **2 extra weeks** for an abnormal delivery or multiple births.

-   A nursing mother may take breaks during working hours to nurse her baby
-   You cannot be dismissed because you are pregnant or on maternity leave

questions: i was sick and my boss deducted pay
intents.answer:
Sick leave terms are usually set by your contract or collective agreement, often supported by a medical certificate. If you are unsure of your rights or think you were treated unfairly, contact your nearest Labour Department office.

If you were injured at work, ask me about **workmen's compensation**.

questions: do i need a written contract
my employer has no contract for me
intents.answer:
For work of 6 months or more, your employer should give you a **written statement of your main terms** (pay, hours, leave, duties, notice) within 2 months of starting.

Keep copies of your contract and payslips. If you have problems, the Labour Department can advise.

questions: how much notice must my employer give
can i be sacked without notice
intents.answer:
Minimum notice under the Labour Act (either side can give pay instead of notice):

-   Contract of **3 years or more**: 1 month's notice or 1 month's pay
-   Contract **under 3 years**: 2 weeks' notice or 2 weeks' pay
-   **Week to week** contract: 7 days' notice

Your contract may give longer notice.

questions: my boss sacked me without notice
they sacked me because i am pregnant
intents.answer:
Termination is **unfair** if it is for reasons such as pregnancy, union membership, filing a complaint, illness, or without a valid reason and fair procedure.

-   Write down what happened and keep your contract, payslips and letters
-   Report to the nearest **Labour Department office** for advice and mediation
-   A Labour Officer will mediate between you and your employer for free

Meanwhile, keep your job search going on GLMIS.

questions: how do i file a labour complaint
where do i report my employer
i want to report my company
how to make a complaint against my boss
intents.answer:
How to resolve a workplace problem:

-   **1.** Raise it with your employer or supervisor, in writing if possible
-   **2.** If unresolved, go to the nearest **Labour Department office** or Public Employment Centre for advice and mediation
-   **3.** If no agreement is reached, the Labour Officer will advise you on your further options under the law

Bring your contract, payslips and any letters.

questions: what is the minimum age to work in ghana
at what age can a child work
intents.answer:
Under the Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560):

-   Minimum age for employment: **15 years**
-   Light work (not harmful, does not affect school): from **13 years**
-   Hazardous work (mining, fishing at sea, heavy loads, chemicals, night work): **18 years**
-   No child may do night work between **8pm and 6am**

questions: how do i report child labour
my 12 year old nephew is working in a mine
a child is being forced to work
children carrying loads at the market
intents.answer:
Thank you for speaking up. Children under 18 must never do hazardous work such as mining or galamsey. You can report to:

-   The **Child Labour Unit** of the Labour Department, or any Labour Department office
-   Your **District Assembly** or Department of Social Welfare
-   The **Police** (DOVVSU), especially if the child is in immediate danger

Give the location and what you saw. You do not need proof to report.

questions: what is the ghana accelerated action plan against child labour
what is government doing about child labour
intents.answer:
The **Ghana Accelerated Action Plan Against Child Labour (2023-2027)** guides national efforts to end child labour, working with District Assemblies, communities, employers, cocoa and mining sectors, and partners.

The Labour Department's Child Labour Unit coordinates much of this work.

Under the **Workmen's Compensation Law, 1987 (PNDCL 187)**, a worker injured (or the family of a worker killed) in a work accident may be compensated:

-   The employer must report the accident to the **Labour Department**
-   The worker has a medical assessment of the injury
-   The Department assesses the claim and the **employer or its insurer pays**

Get medical care first, then contact your nearest office.

Employers must provide a **safe and healthy workplace**: safe equipment, training, and protective equipment (PPE) where needed, at no cost to the worker.

A worker may report unsafe conditions to the Labour Department, and should not be punished for doing so.

questions: does the labour department inspect workplaces
what happens during a labour inspection
intents.answer:
Labour Officers carry out **workplace inspections** to check that employers follow the law on wages, hours, leave, safety, child labour and records.

Employers should keep proper records and cooperate. Workers can request an inspection by reporting a problem to their nearest office.

questions: what are my obligations as an employer
intents.answer:
Key employer duties include:

-   Pay at least the minimum wage, on time
-   Respect hours, leave and maternity rights
-   Give written terms of employment
-   Keep a safe workplace and report accidents
-   Never employ children in prohibited work

Recruit for free on **GLMIS**.

questions: can i join a trade union
my boss says i cannot join a union
intents.answer:
Workers in Ghana have the right to form or join a **trade union** of their choice. Dismissing or punishing a worker for union membership is unfair.

Collective agreements can give better terms than the legal minimum.

questions: i want to open a recruitment agency
how to license a private employment agency
intents.answer:
To operate a **private employment agency** you need a licence:

-   Register your company with the **Registrar-General**
-   Apply to the Minister through the **Labour Department**
-   Your premises and staff are inspected
-   If approved, a licence is issued
-   Submit **quarterly returns within 14 days** after each quarter

Operating without a licence is illegal.

questions: an agent wants money for a visa job
how do i know if an agency is licensed
intents.answer:
**Be careful.** Warning signs of a recruitment scam:

-   You must pay money for a "visa lottery", processing or a guaranteed job
-   No written contract, or the agency has no licence
-   Pressure to travel quickly or hand over your passport

Only use **licensed** agencies and verify them with the Labour Department before paying or travelling. Genuine local jobs are on GLMIS for free.

questions: how to travel to work outside ghana safely
intents.answer:
If you plan to work abroad:

-   Use only a **licensed private employment agency**; verify it with the Labour Department
-   Get a written contract before you travel and keep a copy with family
-   Never hand your passport to an agent you cannot verify

Also explore opportunities at home on **GLMIS**.

questions: who is the chief labour officer
intents.answer: The **Chief Labour Officer** is **Braimah Ibrahim Dawuda**, who heads the Labour Department of Ghana.

questions: what does the labour department do
what is the labour department of ghana
intents.answer: The **Labour Department** administers labour laws in Ghana. We run Public Employment Centres and GLMIS, inspect workplaces, settle complaints, license private employment agencies, handle workmen's compensation and fight child labour.

questions: which ministry is the labour department under
ministry of labour toll free number
intents.answer:
The Labour Department is under the **Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment**.

-   Toll-free: **0800 600 300** or **0800 600 400**
-   Website: melr.gov.gh

questions: what is the new labour bill
is there a new labour law
intents.answer: A **new Labour Bill** is being developed to update the Labour Act, including protections for gig, platform and remote workers. It is **not yet law**, so the Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651) still applies.

questions: where can i read your news
latest news from the labour department
intents.answer: Our **News and guides** page has plain-language guides on finding work, your rights and job fairs. You can share any guide straight to WhatsApp or Facebook.

questions: how do i contact the labour department
intents.answer:
Our offices are open **Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm** (closed on public holidays). There is a Labour Department office or Public Employment Centre in every region.

-   Toll-free: **0800 600 300** or **0800 600 400**
-   Email: **info@labourdepartment.gov.gh**
